title: Cast-Iron Pan Pizza
cScaleSummary: C3 because the recipe contains cholesterol from the Italian sausage, pepperoni, and part-skim mozzarella cheese. The restrained portion sizes keep the overall cholesterol moderate for a full pizza.
ldlActiveSummary: Not LDL-Active because the recipe is designed as a controlled-indulgence pizza rather than an LDL-lowering recipe. While the olive oil, mushrooms, onion, and jalapeño contribute beneficial plant ingredients, the sausage, pepperoni, and cheese shift the recipe away from LDL-active design principles.
intro: Cast-iron pan pizza borrows from several American pizza traditions at once. The heavy skillet creates a crust that fries lightly in olive oil while staying airy and chewy inside, somewhere between tavern pizza, Sicilian pan pizza, and old-school home oven pie. This version keeps the topping balance restrained and deliberate so every ingredient earns its place: concentrated tomato sauce, crisp-edged pepperoni, browned sausage, mushrooms, jalapeños, onion, and just enough cheese to bind everything together without turning greasy.

stepGroups.title: Make the Dough
items: Combine the bread flour ({{quantity:bread-flour}}), water ({{quantity:water}}), olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-dough}}), fine sea salt ({{quantity:salt}}), and instant yeast ({{quantity:instant-yeast}}) in a bowl. Mix until no dry flour remains.
Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Stretch and fold the dough 6 to 8 times in the bowl until smoother and slightly elastic.
Cover and let rise at room temperature for 2 to 3 hours, until puffy and roughly doubled.
Oil a 10-inch cast-iron skillet with the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-pan}}).
Transfer the dough to the skillet and turn it once to lightly coat both sides with oil.
Press the dough outward toward the edges of the skillet. If the dough resists, let it rest for 10 minutes and continue pressing until it fills the pan.
Cover and let rise in the skillet for 45 to 60 minutes until puffy.

stepGroups.title: Make the Sauce
items: Heat the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-sauce}}) in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Add the garlic ({{quantity:garlic}}) and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes ({{quantity:crushed-tomatoes}}), dried oregano ({{quantity:oregano}}), fine sea salt ({{quantity:salt-sauce}}), and black pepper ({{quantity:pepper-sauce}}).
Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and concentrated.
Cool slightly before assembling the pizza.

stepGroups.title: Prepare the Toppings
items: Heat a small skillet over medium heat.
Add the Italian sausage ({{quantity:italian-sausage}}) and break it into small crumbles while cooking until browned and fully cooked through, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Transfer the sausage to paper towels to drain excess fat.

Toss the mushrooms ({{quantity:mushrooms}}), red onion ({{quantity:red-onion}}), and jalapeño ({{quantity:jalapeno}}) with the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-toppings}}), fine sea salt ({{quantity:salt-toppings}}), and black pepper ({{quantity:pepper-toppings}}).

stepGroups.title: Assemble and Bake
items: Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack in the lower third.
Dimple the risen dough gently with oiled fingertips, leaving the outer edge slightly thicker.
Spread the thickened sauce over the dough, leaving a 1/2-inch border around the edge.
Scatter the part-skim mozzarella ({{quantity:mozzarella}}) evenly over the sauce.
Add the browned sausage, mushrooms, red onion, and jalapeño.
Arrange the pepperoni ({{quantity:pepperoni}}) over the top so the edges can crisp during baking.
Bake for 14 to 18 minutes until the cheese is browned in spots, the pepperoni is crisping at the edges, and the crust is deeply golden.
Lift the edge with a spatula and check the underside. If the bottom needs more color or crispness, place the skillet over medium heat on the stovetop for 1 to 3 minutes, rotating as needed.
Rest for 3 minutes in the skillet.
Transfer to a cutting board, finish with the fresh basil ({{quantity:fresh-basil}}), slice, and serve.
